names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 24 martie, «Sfântul Ierarh Artemon, Episcopul Seleuciei».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 24 Μαρτίου, «Όσιος Αρτέμων επίσκοπος Σελευκείας της Πισιδίας», with the rank word and the see left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's first heading for the Julian 24 March on pravoslavno.rs, „Свети Артемон, епископ селевкијски.“, with Свети left off, which is not a rank, and with the see епископ селевкијски left off as well. The heading gives no epithet, so the bare forename is what the source gives. The corpus keeps a second Artemon, of Laodicea, on this same menologion day; he holds no Serbian form, and this one is distinguished from him in the corpus by `display_name` and by slug.

source.text: doxologia.ro, calendarul zilei pentru 24 martie — «Sfântul Ierarh Artemon, Episcopul Seleuciei»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 24ης Μαρτίου — «Όσιος Αρτέμων επίσκοπος Σελευκείας της Πισιδίας»

attestations.note: «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 24 Μαρτίου εκάστου έτους.» The same 24 Μαρτίου keeps a second Artemon, the hieromartyr and presbyter of Laodicea, on a page of his own, and the corpus keeps him too; the see in this line — Σελευκείας της Πισιδίας — is what tells the two apart, and neither row has been written from the other's page. This page gives no year, only «στους αποστολικούς χρόνους», in the apostolic times, so no dates object has been written from it.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 06.04.2026 (24. март ст. ст.) — „Свети Артемон, епископ селевкијски.“

attestations.note: The day's first entry, on the same menologion day the Romanian and the Greek already keep in this folder, and the same bishop: born and brought up at Seleucia, made bishop of that city by the apostle Paul, and dead in deep old age. `paul-the-apostle` is already `related` here in both directions and no row was added. The entry gives no year, no century and no reign, so this folder's `dates` object stays empty, as it was. It calls him a physician of the souls and the bodies of men, and `physician` was **not** taken as a `type` from it: the phrase is a figure for a bishop's care and not the title Лекар that BRIEF-SERBIAN.md §5 maps to that type, and nothing on the page says he practised medicine. saint.gr puts his Seleucia in Pisidia, which the Prologue does not name; nothing was made of that and no `locations` was added. The stored form is the bare forename, because Свети is not a rank and епископ селевкијски is the see this folder keeps in `office`. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the one hymn here is doxologia's.

hymns.text: Θεία Χάριτη ιερατεύσας, φύσιν άλογον, τω ρήματί σου, υπακούουσαν έσχηκας, Άγιε, και εναθλήσας Αρτέμων στερρότατα, διπλών στεφάνων θεόθεν ηξίωσαι, Πάτερ Όσιε, Χριστόν τον θεόν ικέτευε, δωρήσασθαι ημίν το μέγα έλεος.

source.text: saint.gr — Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος γ’, Θείας πίστεως, on the page of Όσιος Αρτέμων επίσκοπος Σελευκείας της Πισιδίας. It names him and is the only hymn the page prints; its accents are copied as the page has them. Two things in it the page's own life does not say — that a brute beast obeyed his word, and that he contended and won a double crown — which is the language of a martyrdom, and this page's Artemon dies in peace. The text is taken whole as his service because it stands under his name, and the discrepancy is recorded here rather than mended.

english.text: Having served as priest by divine grace, thou hadst a brute nature obedient to thy word, O holy one; and having contended most steadfastly, O Artemon, thou wast counted worthy from God of a double crown. O venerable father, entreat Christ God to grant us great mercy.
